texts.full_text: transistors. 2. Description of Related Art For a field-effect transistor (FET), a gate typically controls electrical current that flows between a source and a drain. In a metal-oxide semiconductor field-effect transistor (mOSFET), gate control is achieved by regulating the height of a conduction channel in energy below threshold or through self consistent electrostatics and the number of charge carriers within the conduction channel above a threshold, with the threshold being the point of switching between an ON state and an OFF state of the MOSFET. For a short-channel (i.e., a few tens of nanometers channel length) FET in which gate control is dominated by electrostatics rather than carrier transport through conduction channels, there are several known techniques for enhancing performance: 1 - Strained Silicon Technique This method involves straining the crystal lattice structure to improve electron mobility. By applying a strain (either tensile or compressive), charge carriers can move more freely within strained silicon compared with unstrai\n ed material due its altered band gap and effective mass values, resulting in higher drive currents for improved device performance at lower power consumption levels 2 - High-K Dielectric Technique High dielectric constant materials such as hafnium oxide or zirconium dioxide are used to replace traditional gate oxides made from silicon dioxides/oxynitrides; these high K dielectrics allow thicker physical layers while maintaining equivalent electrical thicknesses thereby reducing leakage current significantly without compromising switching speed 3 - Metal Gate Electrode Technique Using metal gates instead of conventional polysilicon ones can help eliminate issues related to poly depletion effects which degrade MOSFET performance by increasing threshold voltage unpredictably over time due their inherent work function differences with underlying silicon substrate materials; additionally certain metals possess higher conductivities leading up enhanced AC frequency response needed for high speed applications 4 - Fin Structure Technique Incorporating fin structures into FET design effectively increases gate-controlled surface area while maintaining small footprint sizes suitable even ultra dense integrated circuit layouts where traditional planar designs may struggle keeping pace technologically speaking due their inherent size limitations imposed upon them by manufacturing processes available today's market space
